**A stock split is when a company increases the number of its shares by dividing existing ones, lowering the price per share but keeping the overall value of the company the same.** For example, in a 2-for-1 split, each shareholder gets two shares for every one they owned, but each share is worth half as much. Your total investment value doesn’t change — you just own more shares at a lower price.
